newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. might seek to oust Saddam, Kuwait envoy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. might seek to oust Saddam, Kuwait envoy.

text.p: The United States might try to bring about the removal from power of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, Kuwait's ambassador to Washington said in remarks published on Monday.

"Sheikh Mohammad al-Sabah said he has noted that the U.S. policy was inclined to formulate a mechanism to bring about the downfall of the current Iraqi regime," the official Kuwait News Agency said of the envoy's remarks at a seminar by the agency.

The ambassador did not list Washington's steps to end Saddam's rule but said they included the tightening of the noose around the Iraqi leader's neck by the Congress which endorsed a bill urging the White House to try Saddam as a war criminal.
"This, he believed, was an important element in the mechanism now being polarised to cause the downfall of the Iraqi regime," the agency added.

In March, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright affirmed Washington's intentions to back political opposition in Iraq and for the first time announced a clear commitment to improve ties with a new leadership in Baghdad.
The State Department later denied that Albright was urging the overthrow of Saddam.
Washington, which led the 1991 Gulf War, has repeatedly said that toppling Saddam was not among the objectives of the war to free Kuwait of a seven-month Iraqi occupation.
